title: Gamification in mobile-assisted language learning: a systematic review of Duolingo literature from public release of 2012 to early 2020
authors: M. Shortt, S. Tilak, I. Kuznetcova, B. Martens, B. Akinkuolie
note: ANCHOR. The canonical external systematic review: 367 records screened, 35 included. Finds the literature is design-focused, non-probability-sampled and US/English-skewed. The natural baseline to extend to 2026.

title: Mobile-assisted language learning with Babbel and Duolingo: comparing L2 learning gains and user experience
authors: M. Kessler, S. Loewen, T. Gonulal
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. Rare head-to-head external comparison of two commercial adaptive apps.

title: The effects of frequency, duration, and intensity on L2 learning through Duolingo
note: Dose-response analysis; an independent test of the practice-intensity assumption baked into the algorithm.

title: L2 grit and age as predictors of attrition in mobile-assisted language learning
authors: E. Sudina, Y. Teimouri, L. Plonsky
note: Who drops out, and why gamified retention is not learning retention.

title: The Effects of Duolingo, an AI-Integrated Technology, on EFL Learners' Willingness to Communicate and Engagement in Online Classes
authors: Z. Ouyang, Y. Jiang, H. Liu
note: Quasi-experimental (n=40); one of few external studies that explicitly frames Duolingo AS an AI technology.

title: Self-directed language learning with Duolingo in an out-of-class context
note: Interview study on autonomy, motivation and the limits of algorithmic scaffolding.

title: Supporting learners' self-management for self-directed language learning: a study within Duolingo
authors: Z. Li, C.J. Bonk, C. Zhou
note: Self-management scaffolds inside an adaptive app.

title: Impacts of digital applications on emergent multilinguals' language learning experiences: the case of Duolingo
note: Multilingual learner experience.

title: Opening the 'Black Box': How Out-of-Class Use of Duolingo Impacts Chinese Junior High School Students' Intrinsic Motivation for English
note: Self-determination-theory critique of the reward loop.

title: How Effective Is Duolingo at Promoting Implicit Pronunciation Learning?
note: Targets the speech-recognition / pronunciation component specifically.

title: Duolingo-Inspired Pretesting with Words and Pictures Improves Vocabulary Learning
note: Lab replication testing whether the exercise DESIGN, not the AI, drives gains. Methodologically sharp.

title: The Effectiveness of App-Based and Classroom-Based Instruction on L2 Learning and Motivation
authors: B. Gonzalez-Fernandez, I. de la Vina
note: App vs classroom head-to-head.

title: Enhancing willingness to communicate in English among Chinese students in the UK: the impact of MALL with Duolingo and HelloTalk
authors: D. Zhao, R.R. Jablonkai, A. Sandoval-Hernandez
venue: Journal of China Computer-Assisted Language Learning
note: Open access via De Gruyter.

title: Online Learning through Duolingo Stories: An Examination of Literacy Development
note: Same author also has JEO 2024 (teacher assessment) and JEO 2023 (discussion boards during COVID).

title: The Effectiveness of Duolingo English Courses in Developing Reading and Listening Proficiency
authors: X. Jiang, R. Peters, L. Plonsky, B. Pajak
note: CAUTION: mixed authorship - Jiang and Pajak are Duolingo employees. The most-cited 'does it work' paper; treat as partially in-house.

title: The effectiveness of Duolingo in developing receptive and productive language knowledge and proficiency
note: ~27 hours of study yields significant gains across receptive AND productive measures. Open access.

title: A Lesson with Your Artificial Language Tutor: Analyzing Conversational AI in Duolingo, Speakology, and ChatGPT
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. The only external evaluation found that directly examines Duolingo VIDEO CALL alongside competitors.

title: Evaluating LLM-Generated Lessons from the Language Learning Students' Perspective: A Short Case Study on Duolingo
authors: C.R. Catalan, P.N. Monderin, L.M. Dizon, G. Estrella, R.J. Sarmiento, M.A. Patalagsa
note: External student-perspective evaluation of Duolingo's LLM-generated lesson content. Directly probes the AI-course pivot.

title: Uncurtaining windows of motivation, enjoyment, critical thinking, and autonomy in AI-integrated education: Duolingo vs. ChatGPT
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. True experiment, 3 groups (n=81/81/82). No significant difference between Duolingo and raw ChatGPT on critical thinking and autonomy.

title: Gamified and Non-Gamified AI Tools in Enhancing EFL Listening Comprehension: Duolingo and Replika
note: Duolingo vs an LLM companion app on listening outcomes.

title: Duolingo Evolution: From Automation to Artificial Intelligence
authors: J. Vega, M. Rodriguez, E. Check, H.W. Moran, L. Loo
note: External engineering-history account of the automation-to-AI shift. Extended version in Springer CCIS 2025.

title: Evaluating the Impact of AI Tools on Language Proficiency and Intercultural Communication in Second Language Education
venue: International Journal of Second and Foreign Language Education 3(1)
note: Open access.

title: The effects of AI-guided individualized language learning: A meta-analysis
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. The closest thing to a quantitative synthesis of adaptive/AI-personalised language learning. Duolingo is a core included platform.

title: Can Generative AI Chatbots Promote Second Language Acquisition? A Meta-Analysis
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. The benchmark against which Roleplay / Video Call-type features should be judged.

title: Two years of innovation: A systematic review of empirical generative AI research in language learning and teaching (2023-2024)
note: PRISMA, 144 articles. Writing dominates (51.3%); speaking badly under-studied - which is exactly where Video Call sits.

title: Applying Generative AI to Task-based Language Teaching and Learning: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
note: 25 studies, 2,431 participants.

title: A meta-analysis of generative AI effects on language proficiency and affective-cognitive outcomes in language learning
note: Stronger effects in INFORMAL learning settings and for productive skills - directly relevant to an app like Duolingo.

title: A systematic review of AI in second language acquisition using the expanded SAMR model (2015-2024)
note: 281 studies. Useful for classifying Duolingo's AI as augmentation vs redefinition.

title: A PRISMA-based systematic review of artificial intelligence in English as a foreign and second language education (2023-2025)
note: Most recent PRISMA review in the space.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Language Learning: A Twenty-Year Scoping Review of Applications, Research Methods, and Outcomes
note: KEY STAT: Duolingo appears in only 1.4% of empirical AI-in-language-learning studies (2005-2024). The dominant app is drastically under-studied.

title: A Systematic Review of Multilingual Applications, Large Language Models, and Language Learning (2015-2024)
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. 161 studies. Sharpest peer-reviewed critique of Duolingo's streak/reward design; cites the ~12% intermediate-fluency figure.

title: Mobile-assisted language learning with commercial apps: A focused methodological review of quantitative/mixed methods research - and ethics
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. Interrogates the ethics of researching commercial apps, including researcher-company entanglement. Directly relevant to the mixed-authorship problem.

title: Do mobile games improve language learning? A meta-analysis
note: 38 studies, 4,102 participants, g = 0.962.

title: A Meta-Analysis on Mobile-Assisted Language Learning Applications: Benefits and Risks
note: g = 0.88 but flags HIGH risk of bias and low evidence quality across MALL. A good skeptical anchor.

title: Enabling learner independence and self-regulation in language education using AI tools: a systematic review
note: Open access.

title: Integrating Generative AI in Language Education: A Systematic Review of Pedagogical, Ethical, and Technological Themes
note: Open access.

title: Twenty-first century technologies and language education: Charting a path forward
note: The flagship applied-linguistics disciplinary response to commercial AI language tools.

title: Generative artificial intelligence, co-evolution, and language education
note: Companion piece in the same MLJ special issue (see also Davin, 10.1111/modl.12925).

title: Examining the predictive validity of the Duolingo English Test: Evidence from a major UK university
authors: T. Isaacs, R. Hu, D. Trenkic, J. Varga
note: ANCHOR. The definitive independent predictive-validity study. Green OA full text via UCL Discovery.

title: Speaking performances, stakeholder perceptions, and test scores: Extrapolating from the Duolingo English Test to the university
authors: D.R. Isbell, D. Crowther, H. Nishizawa
note: Do AI-scored DET speaking scores translate to real academic speech that faculty accept?

title: Fairness of using different English accents: The effect of shared L1s in listening tasks of the Duolingo English Test
authors: O. Kang, X. Yan, M. Kostromitina, R. Thomson, T. Isaacs
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. The key external accent-bias study on an AI-scored test. Finds a shared-L1 benefit but no penalty for highly intelligible accents.

title: Test Takers' Attitudes Toward Varieties of Accents in Listening Tasks of the Duolingo English Test
authors: O. Kang, M. Kostromitina, X. Yan
note: Attitudinal companion to Kang et al. 2024.

title: Examining the subjective fairness of at-home and online tests: Taking Duolingo English Test as an example
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. Test-takers perceive the DET as invalid even where objective bias analyses find none. Directly on remote AI proctoring and equity.

title: Writing assessment literacy and its impact on the learning of writing: A netnography focusing on Duolingo English Test examinees
note: Washback of AI-scored writing: how examinees reverse-engineer the automated scorer. Excellent angle.

title: Construct representation and predictive validity of integrated writing tasks: the writing component of the Duolingo English Test
note: External construct critique of what the automated writing score actually measures.

title: Exploring the effects of task difficulty and learner variables on performance on picture description writing tasks
note: DET-format task analysis.

title: Predictability of Duolingo English mock test for Chinese college-level EFLs: using assessment use argument
note: Open access.

title: A survey of English language proficiency tests in international student admissions at US research-intensive universities
note: Institutional-uptake evidence: where the DET is and is not accepted.

title: Influences of Duolingo English Test: A Qualitative Study on the Tertiary-Level Students of Bangladesh
note: Global-South access and equity angle.

title: Duolingo English Test vs. IELTS in South Asia: Accessibility, Validity, Cost, and Equity
note: Recent equity-framed comparison. Open access.

title: How Do We Demonstrate AI Responsibility: The Devil Is in the Details
venue: Journal of Educational and Behavioral Statistics
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. External statistician's direct rebuttal to Duolingo's Responsible AI claims. Rare formal scholarly pushback - pair with burstein24rai.

title: When Gamification Spoils Your Learning: A Qualitative Case Study of Gamification Misuse in a Language-Learning App
authors: R. Hadi Mogavi, B. Guo, Y. Zhang, E.-U. Haq, P. Hui, X. Ma
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. The best-known independent critical HCI study of Duolingo's gamification; documents how streaks and leagues displace learning goals.

title: Fair Knowledge Tracing in Second Language Acquisition
authors: W. Tang, G. Chen, S. Zu, J. Luo
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. Fairness audit of models trained on Duolingo SLAM data across platforms and regions. Sits exactly at datasets x ethics.

title: Deep Factorization Machines for Knowledge Tracing
note: Highly cited SLAM-based knowledge tracing, with code.

title: Second Language Acquisition Modeling: An Ensemble Approach
authors: A. Osika, S. Nilsson, A. Sydorchuk, F. Sahin, A. Huss
note: The winning SLAM shared-task system.

title: Variational Deep Knowledge Tracing for Language Learning
note: VDKT on Duolingo data.

title: Deep Knowledge Tracing is an implicit dynamic multidimensional item response theory model
note: Theoretical unification of DKT and IRT; relevant to reverse-engineering Birdbrain.

title: Adaptive and Personalized Exercise Generation for Online Language Learning
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. An independent academic re-implementation of the Duolingo Max content-generation idea, built on Duolingo data.

title: Enhancing human learning via spaced repetition optimization
authors: B. Tabibian, U. Upadhyay, A. De, A. Zarezade, B. Schoelkopf, M. Gomez-Rodriguez
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. The major independent theoretical challenger to half-life regression, using Duolingo's own released traces.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning of Marked Temporal Point Processes
authors: U. Upadhyay, A. De, M. Gomez-Rodriguez
note: Follow-on optimal-review-scheduling work on the same data.

title: Replication of Duolingo's Half-Life Regression in PyTorch
note: Independent reimplementation of Settles & Meeder 2016.

title: Analysis of Half-Life Regression Model Made by Duolingo
note: HIGH-SIGNAL grey literature. Argues HLR's reported gains are partly an artifact of the evaluation setup. Frequently cited in the adaptive-learning community.

title: Predicting and Explaining Behavioral Data with Structured Feature Space Decomposition
authors: P.G. Fennell, Z. Zuo, K. Lerman
note: Uses Duolingo learner behaviour traces.

title: Using Simpson's Paradox to Discover Interesting Patterns in Behavioral Data
authors: N. Alipourfard, P.G. Fennell, K. Lerman
note: Demonstrates aggregation traps in Duolingo-style engagement data. Methodologically useful for critiquing in-house efficacy claims.

title: Question Generation for Adaptive Education
note: Uses SLAM for difficulty-controlled item generation.

title: Are Large Language Models for Education Reliable Across Languages?
note: Uses Duolingo SLAM as a benchmark for cross-lingual educational-LLM reliability. Good multilingual-equity angle.

title: Not Just Duolingo: Supporting Immigrant Language Preservation Through Family-Based Play
authors: A. Ciuba, Z.Y.Y. Li, A. Gautam
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. HCI design critique: Duolingo's individualist, gamified, AI-driven model is inadequate for heritage-language and community needs.

title: Gamification, Motivation, and Contradiction: A Critical Analysis of Duolingo
note: Reads Duolingo through Self-Determination Theory plus dark patterns.

title: Encouraging Repeated App Usage Through Habit-Forming Mechanisms: A Case Study Using the Example of Duolingo
venue: International Journal of Mobile Applications and Technologies
note: Behavioural-design / compulsion-loop analysis. Open access.

title: Revisiting Foucault's panopticon: how does AI surveillance transform educational norms?
authors: British Journal of Sociology of Education
venue: British Journal of Sociology of Education
note: Theoretical frame for AI-proctoring and learning-surveillance critique; applies to DET proctoring.

title: Surveillance Capitalism in Schools: What's the Problem?
note: Cites Duolingo topping an edtech-app study for data collection across 19 segments, sharing identifiers with Facebook. The most concrete academic privacy datapoint found.

title: Duolingo lays off 10% of contractors amid AI push (AI incident record)
note: HIGH-SIGNAL. The canonical institutionally-catalogued record classifying the contractor cuts as an AI labour incident. Citable in policy/ethics writing.

title: English Teachers' Professional Identity in the Age of AI: A Meta-Ethnographic Synthesis
note: Deskilling / identity-disruption framework applicable to the replaces-teachers debate.

title: Professional identity in AI-supported EFL teaching: a comparative qualitative study of pre-service and in-service teachers
note: Open access.

title: Human resource management in the age of generative artificial intelligence
authors: P. Budhwar, S. Chowdhury, G. Wood et al.
note: 800+ citations. The standard scholarly framing for AI-first workforce restructuring. Open access.

title: Campaign Critique: The Strategic 'Marriage' of Duolingo and Luckin Coffee (2025)
venue: Frontiers in Business, Economics and Management
note: Brand/marketing critique; useful for the Duolingo-as-media-company angle. Open access.

title: Simultaneous paraphrasing and translation by fine-tuning Transformer models
note: STAPLE shared-task submission.

title: Machine Translation Robustness to Natural Asemantic Variation
note: Uses STAPLE paraphrase sets as an MT robustness testbed - dataset reuse well beyond education.

title: Growing Together: Modeling Human Language Learning With n-Best Multi-Checkpoint Machine Translation
authors: E.M.B. Nagoudi, M. Abdul-Mageed, H. Cavusoglu
note: STAPLE shared task.

title: Training and Inference Methods for High-Coverage Neural Machine Translation
note: STAPLE submission, hosted on Duolingo's own shared-task site.

title: Duolingo Shared Task on Second Language Acquisition Modeling (Stanford CS230 project report)
note: Student replication. Evidence of the dataset's teaching and benchmark afterlife.
